subject: Hot-path vs Archive: pricing split and dashboard feature gating
messages:
From: Sofía Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@opsgenix.com>, opsgenix-sales@opsgenix.com
Cc: kimberly_park, karthik_iyer
Date: Tue, 04 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hot-path vs Archive: pricing split and dashboard feature gating

Hi Elena / OpsGenix team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a compact pricing workbook (2028-07-04_pricing-model.xlsx) that sketches two primary approaches we discussed for observability add-ons:

1) Split pricing (recommended)
   - Hot-path retention (0-30 days): priced per ingested GB + per-active-dashboard-widget (hot queries optimized for low latency).
   - Cold-archive (30+ days): priced per TB-month; retrievals billed per GB (lower frequency).

2) Unified slab (alternative)
   - Flat slab for retention (tiered by TB/month) with a separate dashboard seat/widget surcharge for high-frequency queries.

Key differentiators in the workbook: how we treat query egress on the hot-path (we recommend capping egress within the hot-tier to protect predictable unit economics), and a feature gate on advanced dashboards (advanced widgets, cross-dataset joins, and anomaly-detectors counted toward "premium widgets").

Questions for you to help narrow the proposal:
- Expected ingested telemetry/day (avg GB) and percent of queries that need sub-100ms hot-path.
- How many named dashboards and estimated premium widgets in month 1/6/12.
- Compliance need for cold-archive retention (do you require >1 year immutable retention or long-term legal hold?).

Ask: If you can share a rough telemetry number and whether procurement prefers a per-GB model or a slab commitment, I’ll produce a clean two-option quote (12 mo / 24 mo commit) and a pilot term sheet.

Thanks,
Sofía Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Sofía Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@opsgenix.com>, opsgenix-sales@opsgenix.com
Cc: kimberly_park, karthik_iyer
Date: Wed, 05 Jul 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hot-path vs Archive: pricing split and dashboard feature gating

Elena — great questions. Short answers inline, longer notes below. I’ve attached a SOW draft (2028-07-05_SOW-draft.pdf) that includes pilot success criteria.

1) Hot-path query egress: the per-active-widget charge covers UI licensing and a moderate number of cached hot queries per widget. Uncached large exports (full dataset dumps) are billed separately as egress. We can set a pilot cap on uncached egress to avoid surprises.

2) Compliance / immutable retention: yes — cold-archive supports WORM-style retention with audit logs and an exportable chain-of-custody. We’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and the audit log extracts for ingestion/export events.

3) Pilot pricing proposal (we recommend to Procurement):
   - 2-month pilot on hosted Redwood with:
     * Hot-path retention for up to 4 TB/month ingested telemetry,
     * Up to 10 dashboards (20 premium widgets),
     * Dedicated SLIs for dashboard latency.
   - Pilot price: 25% of the normalized 12-month committed rate (we can go deeper on discounts if you commit to 12 months afterwards).
   - Uncached export egress cap for pilot: 200 GB (overage at $0.08/GB).

If that looks acceptable I’ll circle back with a formal pricing table and a short pilot term sheet.

Thanks,
Sofía


From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Elena Martin <elena@opsgenix.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer
Date: Thu, 06 Jul 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hot-path vs Archive: pricing split and dashboard feature gating

Elena / Sofía — adding a couple of commercial guardrails from pricing ops:

• Discount bands: 12-month commit -> standard 10% off list for add-ons; 24-month commit -> 18% off; multi-product enterprise commit (Redwood API + Dedicated + Observability bundle) -> bespoke discounts and potential crediting of onboarding fees.
• Pilot concession: we can offer a steeper pilot concession (up to 75% off the normalized rate) if OpsGenix signs a statement of intent to convert to a paid 12-mo agreement within 45 days of pilot completion.
• Dedicated vs Hosted: pricing for the Dedicated deployment will include a baseline seat/instance fee — if you need dedicated GPUs for heavy ad-hoc analytic loads we should price separately.
• Compliance artifacts: I’ll attach SOC2 evidence and the audit-log export template once procurement signs an NDA (we typically exchange these through a secure share).

Action: Sofía, can you include the 12/24 mo pricing table and the DocuSign link for the pilot term sheet? Elena, if procurement can confirm the telemetry volumes and the business owner for dashboard SLIs we’ll finalize the term sheet.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
